subject: Post-call: pricing & burst/quota clarification for Acme Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Santiago <ellie@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Tom Wu <tom.wu@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2025-11-04T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: pricing & burst/quota clarification for Acme Health

Hi Ellie / Tom —

Thanks again for the 30-minute discovery earlier. This thread is a brief recap + a few follow-ups so we can align on pricing/limits and get you a formal proposal quickly. High-level notes from the call: 

- Current expected average: ~25M tokens/month for the pilot MVP.
- Peak/burst patterns: internal events may cause short bursts up to 1.2–1.5M tokens/hour (spiky, ~2–4 hours on those days).
- Growth expectation: ~2–3x within 6 months if initial metrics look good.
- Target unit economics (what you asked us to optimize for): target price of ~$350–$450 per 1M tokens, ideally closer to the low end with a committed/stepped model.

Open items for you to confirm so we can finalize numbers: 
1) Can you confirm average vs peak: is 25M/month the expected baseline consumption? Are the 1.2–1.5M/hour bursts accurate or do you expect larger spikes?
2) Budget range: you mentioned a target spend of $10k–$12k/month in the pilot — is that a hard cap or a flexible target?
3) Rate-limit tolerance: what happens to user experience if we throttle during bursts? Do you need guaranteed concurrency or are client-side retries acceptable?

Next steps from our side: I will loop in Rishi (SE) and Monica (AE) to propose a short-term price+quota plan that meets your target $/1M tokens and outlines our overage / burst handling approach (quota increase turnaround, temporary burst allowances, overage rates). Expect a proposed one-page term sheet + pricing sheet attached.

I attached our latest pricing sheet and the token estimate workbook we used during the call. Please reply if any of the numbers above need correction.

Best,
Marissa Cole

marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: pricing & burst/quota clarification for Acme Health

Hi Marissa —

Thanks — quick clarifications below: 

1) Baseline: yes, 25M tokens/month is the best estimate for phase 1 (pilot). We expect weekends to be lighter; weekday usage is where the bulk comes from.
2) Bursts: our internal notification campaigns create spikes. We saw in our test harness up to ~1.6M tokens in a 1-hour window once (rare), but typical bursts are 800k–1.2M tokens/hour. Important: some of those spikes are unpredictable and we need short-lived headroom without long procurement cycles.
3) Budget: $10k–$12k/month is the comfortable pilot range for procurement, but if unit economics hit your $350/1M target we can stretch to $15k for ramp. 
4) Throttling: user experience can tolerate brief throttles (2–3s extra latency) for non-critical flows; however, for the real-time triage flow (10% of traffic) we need higher priority and low-latency. We need to understand priority routing / rate limits per route.

From procurement: procurement@acmehealth.com asks that any overage charges be capped or tiered so we can forecast spend — a flat surprise overage is a hard no. Also, they prefer a 3-month ramp plan for committed capacity (step-up commitments).

If you can provide a concrete proposal that includes: committed bands (tokens/month), step-up schedule, burst allowance policy, and overage caps/tiers, we’ll review internally and get procurement looped for a quick PO.

Thanks,
Ellie Santiago
Product Lead, Acme Health
ellie@acmehealth.com

Rishi / Monica — forwarding the thread and Ellie's reply. Key asks:
- Pilot baseline 25M/month, rare spikes up to ~1.6M tokens/hr, typical bursts 800k–1.2M/hr.
- Procurement wants overage caps / tiered overage and a 3-month step-up plan.
- Target unit economics: $350/1M ideally.

Suggested approach (first pass):
1) Offer a stepped reserved plan: Month 1 commit 25M tokens @ $325/1M (intro pilot discount), Month 2 commit 40M total @ $300/1M, Month 3 commit 60M @ $280/1M. This achieves an effective blended rate under $320/1M if they step up.
2) Burst allowance: include a free burst buffer equal to 30% of committed throughput per rolling 24h window (to cover short spikes). For larger bursts beyond the buffer, allow temporary quota increases (manual/auto) with a 1–3 business day turnaround for increases >2x baseline; immediate auto-bursts up to 2x baseline per minute but subject to rate limiting and priority buckets.
3) Overage pricing: tiered overage where the first 10% over commitment is billed at +20% (e.g., if committed $300/1M, first overage billed at $360/1M), next 20% at +40%, and full-market rate thereafter. Also include a monthly cap option (e.g., cap spend at +30% of committed spend) if procurement wants predictability for an ARR conversion.

Attached draft pricing sheet and a one-page step-up schedule. If you both agree, I’ll send this proposal to Ellie + procurement and include the DocuSign link for a 3-month PO path.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf, acme_mvp_token_estimates.xlsx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: pricing & burst/quota clarification for Acme Health

Thanks — quick technical notes to include in the proposal so procurement has clarity on rate-limit behavior and SLAs: 

- Rate limits & headers: we will return X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, and Retry-After headers for all requests; these can be used by the client to gracefully back off.
- Priority routing: recommend creating two routes for them: 
  * high-priority route (real-time triage) with a higher reserved concurrency and stricter latency SLO (SLA option)
  * standard route with burst buffer described above
- Burst handling: auto-burst allowance up to 2x the committed per-minute QPS, subject to token budget; sustained bursts that exceed the rolling 24h burst buffer will be throttled.
- Quota increases: small temporary increases (<25% of committed) can be provisioned within minutes via console; increases >25% require manual approval and typically take 1–3 business days depending on GPU capacity. Document this in the SOW.
- Metering & invoices: billable tokens are rounded to the nearest 1k tokens; we provide a monthly consumption report and per-route token breakdown in the Console.

If we price as Marissa suggested, we should also include an explicit overage cap option in the commercial terms (e.g., cap monthly overage charges at 30% of committed spend) to satisfy procurement. I can add the technical appendix for the SOW.

Rishi
